debate.text: Nesterby has £90,000 for 1,100 struggling homes that need £300,000. £82 each is under the £200 floor the citizens set. £300 for 300 homes leaves 800 with nothing. A loan repaid from the gritting budget moves the bill to next winter. Nothing signed. The jury split 4, 4 and 3, so no line is clear enough to bend.

Mira, the gritting lorries are mine, so let me be plain. A loan repaid from the grit budget is a loan repaid from the road to the hospital in February. A bus that cannot get up the hill is no use to a cold house. I back the citizens on that red line.

Look at it from the door. A tenant who gets £82 and a leaflet is a tenant who is behind by March. Hollinwick's arrears came from exactly that squeeze. If the fund stays this small, say so, and do not call £82 help.

Right, Bea. And Elderbrook shows the other way: £160 a home and 150 fixed houses was a trial, not a cure. Here we do not have the money even for a trial. That is what a sent-back day is for. The citizens must choose what gives.
